title: Volume of prisms and cylinders
goal: I can find the volume of prisms and cylinders and change units.
teach: For any right prism or cylinder: volume = area of base × height. A cylinder has V = πr²h. 1 cm³ = 1 mℓ, 1 000 cm³ = 1 litre and 1 m³ = 1 000 litres.
tvis: V = π(4)²(7) = 351,86 cm³.

ex.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 7 cm, in cm³ and in litres. Give answers correct to two decimal places.

watch: Volume is in cubic units; check that all lengths use the same unit first.

qs.text: A triangular prism: the triangle has base 6 cm and height 4 cm; the prism is 10 cm long
qs.hint: Volume = area of the triangle × length.
qs.steps:
1. Formulas (right prism): SA = 2 × base area + perimeter of base × height; V = base area × height. Box: SA = 2(lb + lh + bh); V = l × b × h.
2. Base area = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 cm²
3. V = 12 × 10 = 120 cm³

qs.text: A cylinder with r = 3 cm and h = 10 cm
qs.steps:
1. Formulas (cylinder): SA = 2πr² + 2πrh; curved surface = 2πrh; V = πr²h.
2. V = π(3)²(10) = 90π
3. = 282,74 cm³

qs.text: A cylinder with diameter 10 cm and h = 12 cm
qs.steps:
1. Formulas (cylinder): SA = 2πr² + 2πrh; curved surface = 2πrh; V = πr²h.
2. r = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm
3. V = π(5)²(12) = 300π = 942,48 cm³
